:::{#rem-flexibility}
#### Polynomial degree orders flexibility

Least-squares polynomial fits are ordered by degree:
a polynomial of degree $\polydeg$ is also a polynomial of degree $\polydeg + 1$
whose coefficient of $\predvar^{\polydeg + 1}$ is zero,
so the fit of degree $\polydeg + 1$ is [at least as flexible](#def-flexibility)
as the fit of degree $\polydeg$.
The four fits of @exr-overfitting are ordered this way.
@def-flexibility is narrower than the informal use of the word
in @james2021islr2e [sec. 2.1.3]:
it orders only procedures whose candidate sets are nested.
Other procedures can be compared by other measures,
such as the effective number of parameters
[@hastie2009elements, sec. 7.6].

:::
